shorts.title: Omar After Federal Search: "I Will Not Be Silenced" #Shorts
shorts.narration: [serious] Folks, federal agents searched Congresswoman Ilhan Omar's home on Monday. Her answer was short. [beat] "I will not be silenced." [serious] The Justice Department says Homeland Security agents executed a judicially authorized search warrant in an ongoing federal criminal investigation, and it gave no other details. Omar calls it an attempt to "weaponize federal law enforcement." She denies the immigration fraud claims Vice President Vance has made. [sarcastic] Jeffries and top Democrats say a "violent mass deportation machine" descended on her home. [beat] Over a warrant a judge authorized. [deadpan] Democrats love judges. Right up until one signs something. [warm] Proverbs 18:17 says, "He that is first in his own cause seemeth just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him." [beat] Let the facts come out. [mischievously] Democrats, be honest: if this were a Republican's house, would you be this upset? Tell me below, and subscribe. Henry roasts the news every day.

claims.text: Federal agents searched the Washington-area home of Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) on Monday, Oct. 12, 2026; the Justice Department said Homeland Security Investigations agents executed a judicially authorized search warrant related to an ongoing federal criminal investigation and gave no other details.
Omar wrote on X "I will not be silenced" and called the search an "attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement."

Omar and her office have called the immigration-fraud claims false; Vice President Vance said in March, without offering evidence, that the administration believed Omar 'definitely committed immigration fraud'.
Jeffries and other top Democrats said in a joint statement that Trump's "violent mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family."
A DOJ spokesperson said the search was carried out under a judicially authorized warrant secured by the Department of Justice, and the DOJ described the investigation as criminal.

shorts.title: Montana Dem Chair Quits, Backs Someone Else For Senate #Shorts
shorts.hook: Dem Chair Quits, Endorses Her Rival
shorts.narration: [incredulous] Folks, the Montana Democratic Party chairwoman just quit. And then she endorsed somebody who isn't her party's nominee. [beat] Shannon O'Brien resigned Monday and backed independent Seth Bodnar over Democratic nominee Alani Bankhead. [serious] In her op-ed she said her party is "more divided than ever." Former Governor Steve Bullock, former Senator Jon Tester and former Senator Max Baucus had already backed Bodnar. [sarcastic] So the Democrats' own chair, and three of their big names, are campaigning against the Democrat. [beat] That's not a party. That's a group chat that's muted the nominee. [warm] Mark 3:25 says, "And if a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand." [beat] Somebody should tell the Democrats it's not a suggestion. [mischievously] Democrats, who's the real nominee in Montana? Argue it out below, and subscribe. Henry roasts the news every day.

claims.text: Shannon O'Brien resigned as chair of the Montana Democratic Party on Oct. 12, 2026 and endorsed independent Senate candidate Seth Bodnar over Democratic nominee Alani Bankhead.
O'Brien wrote that the party is "more divided than ever — not because of our values but because of the race for the U.S. Senate."
Former Gov. Steve Bullock, former Sen. Jon Tester and former Sen. Max Baucus had already backed Bodnar.
Montana Democratic Party chair Shannon O'Brien resigned and endorsed independent Seth Bodnar over the Democratic nominee, Alani Bankhead.

slides.speaker: Shannon O'Brien, outgoing Montana Democratic Party chair

slides.label: Big-name Democrats who backed the independent

shorts.title: Trump In Alaska: Vote For "The Real Dan Sullivan" #Shorts
shorts.narration: [amused] Folks, there are two Dan Sullivans on the Alaska ballot. And President Trump flew to Wasilla on Tuesday to tell voters which is which. [beat] "The real Dan Sullivan." [serious] Trump was rallying for Republican Senator Dan Sullivan against Democrat Mary Peltola. A second candidate is listed as Daniel J. Sullivan, and Trump and Republicans accuse Democrats of backing him to confuse voters. Trump made that claim at the rally. [sarcastic] Democrats, of course, have Peltola ahead by 1.4 points in the RealClearPolitics average. [beat] Which is awfully close to the margin of confusion. [deadpan] It's a tough break when your best strategy is a name tag mix-up. [warm] Matthew 7:15 says, "Beware of false prophets." [beat] In Alaska, beware of false Sullivans. [mischievously] Democrats, if it's all a coincidence, why won't you say so? Tell me below, and subscribe. Henry roasts the news every day.

claims.text: On Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026, President Trump held a rally in Wasilla, Alaska, for Sen. Dan Sullivan (R-AK) and other down-ballot Republicans, as the first stop of a western tour.
Another candidate named Dan Sullivan, listed on the ballot as "Daniel J. Sullivan," is also running; Trump and Republicans accuse Democrats of backing him to confuse voters.
Before the rally, former Rep. Mary Peltola, the Democratic candidate, led Sullivan by 1.4 points in the RealClearPolitics polling average.
Trump urged voters to back "the real Dan Sullivan" (headline of the article); the article reports his claims about the other candidate without independent verification.
